summary.en: The Philippine Coast Guard contained a 2,000‑liter mineral oil leak from an NGCP submarine cable off Tabango, Leyte, and recovered 250 kilograms of oil waste, while Japan pledged $27 million for coastal radar and drones to enhance Philippine surveillance. China Coast Guard vessels patrolled waters around the disputed Diaoyu Dao and a Chinese survey ship entered Scarborough Shoal, prompting the Philippines to summon the Chinese ambassador over remarks it deemed threatening. The Philippines also sought additional Indian BrahMos missiles to strengthen its coastal defenses against China. 176 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Den filippinske kystvakten stoppet et 2 000‑liter mineraloljelekkasje fra en NGCP-undervannskabel utenfor Tabango, Leyte, og hentet 250 kilogram oljesøppel, mens Japan lovet 27 millioner dollar til kystradar og droner for å styrke filippinsk overvåkning. Kystvakten i Kina patruljerte farvannene rundt den omstridte Diaoyu-øya, og et kinesisk oppmålingsskip gikk inn i Scarborough-revet, noe som fikk Filippinene til å innkalle den kinesiske ambassadøren over bemerkninger de anså som truende. Filippinene søkte også flere indiske BrahMos-missiler for å styrke kystforsvaret mot Kina. 176 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Moro conflict
background.extract: The Moro conflict was an insurgency in the Mindanao region in southern Philippines which involved multiple armed groups. A decades-long peace process has resulted in peace deals between the Philippine government and two major armed groups, the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), but other smaller armed groups continue to exist. In 2017, the peace council settled around 138 clan conflicts.
